title: Tonelli and finiteness for nonnegative integrals
statement:
Use $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field]. Let $(X,\mu)$ and $(Y,
u)$ be sigma-finite measure spaces, and let $H:X	imes Y	o[0,\infty]$ be measurable up to a set of product measure zero. Nonnegative integrals, with $0\cdot\infty=0$, satisfy
$$\int_{X	imes Y}H\,d(\mu	imes
u)=\int_X\int_Y H(x,y)\,d
u(y)\,d\mu(x)=\int_Y\int_X H(x,y)\,d\mu(x)\,d
u(y).$$
The inner integral in each order is measurable up to a null set. For any measure space $(Z,ho)$ and nonnegative function $h:Z	o[0,\infty]$ measurable up to a null set, $\int h\,dho<\infty$ implies $h<\infty$ almost everywhere. Nonnegative integration is monotone under almost-everywhere inequalities and commutes with multiplication by a fixed nonnegative finite scalar.
